summary: Adds a novel top-level command `garmin-pp-cli insights` with two subcommands, `sleep` and `training` (internal/cli/garmin_insights.go), registered beside the generated analytics command at internal/cli/root.go with a single AddCommand line and a two-line comment. No generated file's behaviour was changed. WHY THE PRESS CANNOT EXPRESS THIS: the generated `analytics` command answers exactly two shapes -- count rows of one resource type, and group rows of one resource type by one JSON field (internal/cli/analytics.go, runGroupBy). Both are single-resource and single-field by construction. Every question these recipes answer spans several resource types at once and needs arithmetic the group-by has no vocabulary for: `insights sleep` joins sleep_stats with sleep_score and computes duration, stage split, a share-of-total, a trailing seven-day mean and a delta against the equally long window before it; `insights training` joins activities with activity_hr_zones on activity id, buckets by ISO week, and reads max_metrics and intensity_minutes for the same window. The generated command also reads with db.List(resourceType, 0) and filters in Go, so it has no date-window predicate to reuse. WHAT IT DOES: both recipes read ONLY the local archive that `history` writes -- no network call on any path -- and take --days (default 28) plus the generated --db. Output goes through the same helpers the generated commands use (wantsMachineOutput, printJSONFiltered), so --json, --compact, --csv, --select and --agent behave identically to every generated command, and a bare invocation prints the same tab-separated table style. `insights sleep` reports coverage, duration in minutes, sleep score, resting heart rate, the four stage minutes both absolutely and as a share of measured sleep, a trailing seven-day rolling mean for duration and score, and a trend block against the prior window. `insights training` reports coverage, totals, a per-activity-type breakdown (count, minutes, kilometres, average heart rate), the heart-rate zone distribution summed across the window's activities, Monday-started weekly buckets of count/minutes/distance/load, weekly intensity minutes, the VO2 max trend for running and cycling, and the training-readiness trend. FIELD NAMES WERE READ OFF A LIVE ARCHIVE, NOT ASSUMED (2026-09-08, 90-day walk of a populated reference account, 975 rows): sleep_stats carries duration and stages under a `values` object as totalSleepTimeInSeconds, deepTime, lightTime, remTime, awakeTime, sleepScore and restingHeartRate, and the four stage fields are seconds -- deep+light+rem equalled totalSleepTimeInSeconds on all 87 measured nights. sleep_score rows are {calendarDate, value}. max_metrics carries `generic` (running) and `cycling` blocks each with vo2MaxValue. intensity_minutes is one row per WEEK with moderateValue/vigorousValue. activity_hr_zones rows are the wrapper `history` writes: {activityId, hrTimeInZones[{zoneNumber, secsInZone, zoneLowBoundary}], zoneCount}. Activity duration is seconds and distance is metres. HONESTY RULES, which are the reason this is more than a query: (1) an empty archive is never an error -- every count comes back zero, every aggregate comes back JSON null, exit status is 0, and a hint on stderr names `garmin-pp-cli history` (not the generated `sync`, which cannot write these series). (2) A null field is never counted as a zero: every metric reports its own `n`, so an average of two nights cannot be mistaken for an average of twenty-eight. (3) A missing `resources` table -- a database that was never migrated -- reads as an empty archive rather than raising, reusing the generated syncHintMissingTable detector. (4) The zone distribution reports activities_with_zones next to activities, because an activity recorded without a heart-rate strap contributes duration but no zone time and would otherwise silently understate the window. (5) A trend against a window the archive does not reach back into is reported as comparable:false with an explanation, not as a delta from zero. QUERY SHAPE: day-keyed series are read with `resource_type = ? AND id >= ? AND id <= ?`, which rides the resources table's (resource_type, id) primary key -- the day-keyed series store the ISO date as the row id, so lexicographic order is chronological. The activity feed and its zone fan-out are keyed by activity id, so those two read `resource_type = ?` (idx_resources_type) and filter on startTimeLocal in Go. Both plans are asserted by test rather than assumed. CROSS-RECORD DEPENDENCY (N131.4h): garmin_insights.go resolves its default archive through garminArchivePath, which is defined in internal/cli/garmin_sync.go and recorded in garmin-windowed-sync.json. The two records must be re-applied together after a reprint: restoring this file without that one does not compile.
reason: N131.4d, and the N131.1 section 8 Q2 ruling that the tool's differentiating value is local-store-only analytics -- recipes that need years of archived rows and therefore exist in no Garmin Connect read. These two are the first pair from that list: sleep trend, and load plus zone distribution. They are the reason the windowed archive walk (patch garmin-windowed-sync) was built, so the archive now has a consumer that proves it is worth writing.
validated_outcome: go build ./... exit 0, go vet ./... exit 0, go test -count=1 ./... green across 14 packages with 0 FAIL; gofmt -l clean on both new files. Twelve new test functions (fifteen cases counting subtests) cover: both recipes' functional output against a synthetic fixture whose expected means are stated exactly; a night whose values are all null, proving a null never becomes a zero in an average or in a rolling point; an activity outside the window and its zones, proving neither leaks into a total; an activity with no archived zones, proving the understatement is warned about rather than hidden; the trend block against a seeded prior window; Monday-started weekly bucketing across a week boundary; the table renderer; --json, --compact and --agent all producing parseable JSON; and idempotence -- two runs produce byte-identical output and leave the database file unchanged. Negative: an empty archive returns zeros plus the stderr hint at exit 0 for both recipes; a half-populated archive holding sleep scores but no sleep_stats rows answers the score block and warns that duration and stage minutes are missing rather than reporting them as measured zeros; a database whose resources table has been dropped reads as empty rather than raising; --days 0 is rejected. Performance: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN is asserted to show SEARCH rather than SCAN for both query shapes, with the day-range plan required to bound resource_type, and the lower and upper id, and a window-size test proves a seven-day window reads half the rows a fourteen-day window does over the same archive. LIVE: both recipes were run against a 90-day archive of a populated reference account (975 rows, 12 series), built into the session scratchpad with `history --days 90 --db <scratch>` so nothing was written to the account's home. `insights sleep --days 90` reported 87 of 90 nights with stats, duration, score and stages, and correctly reported the prior period as not comparable because the archive does not reach back 180 days. `insights training --days 90` reported 155 activities across 12 activity types, 155 of 155 with archived zones, five zone rows whose shares sum to 100 %, 14 weekly buckets, 14 intensity-minute weeks, 27 VO2-max days (17 running, 20 cycling) and 0 readiness days with its warning. Honest zeros were proved on two archives that hold no series rows: a copy of the owner account's own archive (data-<hash>.db, 0 rows of every resource type -- the no-wearable fixture) and a copy of the reference account's data.db, which held one cached `account` profile row and nothing else. Both recipes exit 0 on both with zero counts, null aggregates, empty row lists and the stderr hint naming `history`. The fully-empty case is also covered by test against a freshly migrated store with no rows at all.
regen_notes: The two recipes depend on the resource types `history` writes (sleep_stats, sleep_score, activities, activity_hr_zones, max_metrics, intensity_minutes, training_readiness). A regen that changes those resource names, or that changes the row id of a day-keyed series away from the ISO date, breaks both the readers and the primary-key query shape. The day-keyed id is what makes the range predicate index-backed; a synthetic id would silently turn every recipe into a table scan, which the performance tests would catch.

OPEN, NOT FIXED HERE: training readiness returns zero rows for every day walked on the reference account, and `history` reports that as sync_warning reason series_returned_no_rows. N131 section 9.2 recorded that the 28-day scopes of training readiness carried data on this same account, so either that data came from a different path or the per-date /metrics-service/metrics/trainingreadiness/{date} variant is not the one that carries it. `insights training` reports readiness as zero days with a warning and deliberately does not substitute another endpoint; resolving the discrepancy is an orchestrator decision recorded on the sync stage.

The recipes read `values.sleepScore` from sleep_stats and fall back to the sleep_score series for a night that has stats without a score. If a regen ever stops archiving one of the two, the other still answers; if both are dropped the score block reports n=0 rather than failing.

`insights` shares the small JSON readers jsonChild/jsonStringField/dayFromValue and the civilDay calendar type with internal/cli/garmin_sync.go and internal/cli/garmin_window.go. Those three files are one novel unit and should be carried forward together.

WHY `insights` COEXISTS WITH THE GENERATED `analytics` RATHER THAN REPLACING IT: `analytics` is the press's generic per-resource summariser over the store; `insights` is two named multi-series recipes (sleep, training) that join series `analytics` has no vocabulary to relate. Both read the same resources table, neither writes, and removing `analytics` would mean editing generated wiring a reprint restores.

N131.4g added --from/--to beside --days on both recipes, per plan section 3's `insights <recipe> --from --to` shape. --days remains the default rolling window; --days combined with a complete --from/--to range is refused rather than silently resolved.
